gap: No result ChatGPT got states, per candidate and from the maker's own page, which connection keeps 8,000 Hz and which replacement switches the board accepts (MonsGeek states 8,000 Hz on cable and 2.4 GHz for the FUN60 Ultra, and guarantees its 0.01 mm step only for the switches it lists; Gamakay's NS75 guide states 8,000 Hz for the cable only).
standout_why: Compared against gamepadsquire.com (cited in chat 2), setupinsider.com and mechanicalkeyboard.net, all opened 2026-11-21. Gamepadsquire already says the AULA F75 HE's 8K is wired-only (1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz) and that the FUN60 Ultra TMR polls 8K on cable and 2.4 GHz and takes 5-pin mechanical switches. Setupinsider already says Redragon's magnetic switches do not fit other brands. Mechanicalkeyboard.net already says to use USB for the AULA's 8K. None of them covers a Gamakay board, the FUN60 Ultra HE-versus-TMR switch split with MonsGeek's stated exclusion, or MonsGeek's 0.01 mm caveat. The idea is therefore partly covered; only the cells for these candidates are new. keebforce.com (cited) failed to open with a certificate error. The pcgamer.com and rtings.com list pages came back as navigation only or without relevant text, so I could not compare against them.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. Every candidate under $100 gets its 8K over the cable, so the under-$50 wired boards (Gamakay NS68 wired $36.79, MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro $37.40, Epomaker HE68 Lite $42.49) compete on equal terms and the NS68 belongs in the table on price. For a shopper who wants 8K without a cable, the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra tri-mode is the only candidate whose maker page I opened that states 8,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz, but MonsGeek's own store showed it unavailable with a waitlist today. Write Gamakay NS75 and NS68 8K claims as wired: I could not open a Gamakay page that states their 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth polling rate.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection (maker)
findings.value: 8,000 Hz in wired or 2.4 GHz wireless mode; no Bluetooth polling rate stated
findings.note: Maker's product page. Sold as USB-C wired only or tri-mode (ANSI); the 4,000 mAh battery and 2.4 GHz receiver come with the tri-mode version only.

findings.label: Switch compatibility, HE versus TMR version (maker)
findings.value: HE version: magnetic switches only. TMR version: magnetic switches plus 5-pin mechanical switches (MagMech)
findings.note: The page also lists LED orientation as north-facing on TMR and south-facing on HE. Third-party magnetic switches are selected in the MonsGeek driver; the page says '5 third-party magnetic switches' in one place and 'six switches (including Akko Glare)' in another.

findings.label: Switch exclusion the maker states
findings.value: Akko Magnetic Creamy Yellow (south-facing magnet, used in M1W HE and M1W V3 HE) is not compatible with the FUN60; check switch polarity before replacing

findings.label: Limit on the 0.01 mm rapid trigger step (maker)
